input: Variant call files and pipeline metrics
output: Filtered and annotated VCFs; QC metrics
selection_rationale: Representative toolkit for reproducible variant calling and post-calling quality filtering.
appropriate_use: Use with validated laboratory pipeline and documented filters.
interpretation_boundary: Not a substitute for case-level clinical interpretation.
key_limitations: Pipeline and parameter dependent; implementation-specific.

primary_purpose: VCF manipulation, normalization, filtering, and summary statistics
selection_rationale: Included as a lightweight, widely used option for normalization, filtering, and inspection of variant calls.
appropriate_use: Use when transparent VCF-level processing or normalization is required.
interpretation_boundary: Does not establish variant validity or pathogenicity.
key_limitations: Command and threshold dependent; requires validated local workflow.

selection_rationale: Included for transparent VCF-level filtering and summary operations in post-calling workflows.
appropriate_use: Use for inspection, filtering, and cohort-level VCF summaries as appropriate.
interpretation_boundary: Does not replace validation of calls or clinical evidence appraisal.
key_limitations: Feature set and outputs depend on VCF quality and local parameters. Maintenance is legacy; bcftools covers many of the same VCF operations.

selection_rationale: Included as a maintained reference ecosystem for genome, gene, transcript, and variant annotation.
appropriate_use: Use when annotation requires explicit genome-build and transcript context.
interpretation_boundary: Transcript annotations are not a clinical classification.
key_limitations: Transcript choice and release changes can alter consequences.

selection_rationale: Included as a core curated reference-sequence source for transcript-aware interpretation.
appropriate_use: Use when documenting transcript accessions and reference sequence context.
interpretation_boundary: A transcript record alone does not determine disease relevance.
key_limitations: Transcript updates and alternative isoforms require explicit selection.

selection_rationale: Included because comprehensive annotation supports transparent transcript and gene context.
appropriate_use: Use when transcript-model provenance must be documented.
interpretation_boundary: Does not determine clinical transcript preference by itself.
key_limitations: Release-specific; transcript-model differences may affect consequence calls.

technical_compatibility: NCBI/Ensembl identifiers. GRCh37 coverage is not universal.
selection_rationale: Included to support consistent transcript selection across RefSeq and Ensembl for clinically relevant reporting.
appropriate_use: Use when a MANE transcript is available and appropriate to the clinical context.
interpretation_boundary: Does not eliminate the need to consider disease-specific transcript conventions.
key_limitations: Coverage is not universal; updates occur over time.

primary_purpose: Population allele-frequency assessment and frequency-based filtering
selection_rationale: Included because large-scale population data can test compatibility of allele frequency with a suspected disease model.
appropriate_use: Use for frequency filtering and ancestry-aware contextual assessment.
interpretation_boundary: Rarity or absence does not establish pathogenicity.
key_limitations: Uneven ancestry representation, coverage differences, founder effects, and no phenotype linkage.

technical_compatibility: Public allele-frequency browser (Bravo). Program description: https://topmed.nhlbi.nih.gov/. Controlled-access freezes are distinct from the public browser. GRCh37 availability depends on the release.
selection_rationale: Included as a complementary large-scale frequency resource. The catalogued URL is the public Bravo browser of TOPMed allele frequencies.
appropriate_use: Use when its cohort composition and release are relevant to the frequency question.
interpretation_boundary: Frequency alone is not clinical evidence of pathogenicity.
key_limitations: Population representation and dataset-specific processing must be considered.

primary_purpose: Population genetic variation and ancestry context
selection_rationale: Included as a foundational multi-population reference dataset for complementary frequency and ancestry context.
appropriate_use: Use as complementary context rather than sole frequency evidence.
interpretation_boundary: Does not establish pathogenicity or fully represent all populations.
key_limitations: Limited sample sizes for rare-variant inference relative to newer datasets.

selection_rationale: Included to provide population-relevant frequency context when patient ancestry is appropriately matched.
appropriate_use: Use as complementary evidence for appropriately matched Iranian cases.
interpretation_boundary: Should not be assumed to represent all Iranian or neighboring populations.
key_limitations: Sampling, coverage, and representativeness limitations.

analytical_function: Phenotype encoding and phenotype-driven gene prioritization
primary_purpose: Standardized phenotype encoding and phenotype comparison
input: Clinical features encoded as HPO terms
output: Ontology terms and phenotype similarity context
selection_rationale: Included because structured phenotype encoding supports reproducible phenotype–gene and phenotype–disease comparison.
appropriate_use: Use when clinical findings can be captured with sufficiently specific and temporally appropriate terms.
interpretation_boundary: Phenotype similarity does not independently establish gene–disease causality or variant pathogenicity.
key_limitations: Incomplete, nonspecific, or inaccurately captured phenotypes reduce performance.

analytical_function: Phenotype encoding and phenotype-driven gene prioritization
input: HPO terms; variant data; pedigree where applicable
technical_compatibility: VCF plus phenotype inputs Documentation tracks application release 15.1.1; phenotype and genome data bundles are versioned separately.
selection_rationale: Included as a representative phenotype-driven prioritization platform that integrates phenotype and variant context.
appropriate_use: Use for candidate prioritization when structured phenotype and compatible variant data are available.
interpretation_boundary: Ranking is not proof of causality or classification.
key_limitations: Dependent on phenotype quality, knowledgebase coverage, inheritance assumptions, and model configuration.

analytical_function: Phenotype encoding and phenotype-driven gene prioritization
input: HPO terms; genotype information when available
selection_rationale: Included as a complementary phenotype-driven method emphasizing explicit likelihood-based reasoning.
appropriate_use: Use when transparent phenotype-based diagnostic prioritization is desired.
interpretation_boundary: Output does not independently prove causal variant status.
key_limitations: Sensitive to phenotype completeness, disease annotations, and input assumptions.

analytical_function: Phenotype encoding and phenotype-driven gene prioritization
technical_compatibility: HPO term input; web/API where available
selection_rationale: Included as a focused phenotype-to-gene prioritization option.
appropriate_use: Use for rapid gene prioritization from structured phenotypes.
interpretation_boundary: Does not provide variant classification.
key_limitations: Limited by phenotype encoding and underlying gene–phenotype knowledge.

analytical_function: Gene–disease association assessment;Clinical evidence retrieval and curation
primary_purpose: Gene–disease validity and curated evidence for clinical interpretation
output: Curated gene–disease validity assertions and supporting evidence summaries
selection_rationale: Included because ClinGen expert curation supports gene–disease validity assessment and evidence review when a current assertion exists.
appropriate_use: Use for gene–disease validity and related curated evidence when current curation exists. Gene- and disease-specific classification specifications are the separate ClinGen specifications entry.
interpretation_boundary: Coverage is incomplete. A validity or evidence assertion does not classify the variant under review and does not replace case-specific appraisal.
key_limitations: Curation status and coverage evolve. This entry does not contain the gene-specific ACMG/AMP specifications, which are catalogued separately.

selection_rationale: Included as a widely used gene–phenotype knowledge source for evaluating clinical relevance.
appropriate_use: Use to contextualize known gene–disease relationships and inheritance patterns.
interpretation_boundary: Does not replace formal validity assessment or case-specific classification.
key_limitations: Curation depth and update timing vary by entry.

output: Rare disease and gene association context
selection_rationale: Included for rare-disease nomenclature and gene–disease context.
appropriate_use: Use when rare-disease terminology and cross-referenced disease context are needed.
interpretation_boundary: Does not independently establish causality in an individual case.
key_limitations: Coverage, curation, and update timing vary.

selection_rationale: Included because diagnostic panel curation can provide disease-specific gene relevance context.
appropriate_use: Use as a complementary source when panel evidence and panel scope are relevant.
interpretation_boundary: Panel inclusion is not synonymous with definitive causality or variant pathogenicity.
key_limitations: Panel content and evidence ratings change; jurisdiction-specific practices may differ.

primary_purpose: Integrative prediction of potential variant deleteriousness
selection_rationale: Included as a representative broad variant-effect predictor.
appropriate_use: Use as one supportive computational feature when applicable to the variant class.
interpretation_boundary: Score alone is not clinical pathogenicity evidence.
key_limitations: Model and training-data dependence; calibration and applicability vary by context.

selection_rationale: Included as a representative ensemble predictor for missense variants.
appropriate_use: Use only for applicable missense variants and with gene/disease mechanism context.
interpretation_boundary: Do not treat concordance with related predictors as independent evidence.
key_limitations: Training-data overlap, calibration, and gene/variant-specific performance limitations.

technical_compatibility: Protein/variant input. Genome build is inherited from the annotation implementation.
selection_rationale: Included as a commonly used conservation/function-based missense predictor.
appropriate_use: Use as one supporting predictor for applicable missense variants.
interpretation_boundary: Not a stand-alone clinical classification method.
key_limitations: Limited scope; performance and dependence on shared features must be considered. The public website returned an error on a 2026-10-10 check.

technical_compatibility: Protein/variant input. Genome build is inherited from the annotation implementation.
selection_rationale: Included as a historical and commonly used missense-effect predictor.
appropriate_use: Use as supportive context for applicable missense variants.
interpretation_boundary: Not independent confirmation when used with overlapping predictors.
key_limitations: Variant- and gene-specific performance; limited clinical specificity.

technical_compatibility: Protein or transcript input. The catalogued URL is a public browser of the AlphaMissense score set (Cheng et al. 2023), which is separate from AlphaFold DB.
selection_rationale: Included as a modern missense-focused predictor that may add complementary computational context.
appropriate_use: Use for applicable missense variants with explicit transcript/protein mapping.
interpretation_boundary: Do not use as autonomous clinical classification evidence.
key_limitations: Model applicability, calibration, and biological/clinical context remain limiting.

output: Splice alteration delta scores and positions
selection_rationale: Included as a representative splice-effect predictor for variants with plausible splicing consequences.
appropriate_use: Use with explicit transcript selection and consideration of relevant splice mechanisms.
interpretation_boundary: Prediction is not direct proof of aberrant splicing or clinical pathogenicity.
key_limitations: Tissue, transcript, mechanism, and calibration dependence.

technical_compatibility: Sequence-based input. Build is implied by the sequence context supplied to the scorer. The original Burge-lab score scripts have been intermittently unavailable; this entry cites the method paper.
selection_rationale: Included as a complementary sequence-based splicing assessment method.
appropriate_use: Use for relevant canonical or near-canonical splice-site questions.
interpretation_boundary: Does not demonstrate in vivo splicing outcome.
key_limitations: Limited representation of tissue-specific and broader regulatory context.

technical_compatibility: Database/annotation integration. v1.1 contains GRCh37 coordinates and GRCh38 coordinates lifted from GRCh37.
selection_rationale: Included as a supplementary source of precomputed splicing prediction context.
appropriate_use: Use as complementary computational information for applicable SNVs.
interpretation_boundary: Not direct experimental evidence of aberrant splicing.
key_limitations: Scope is limited to consensus-region SNVs and to the underlying models. The scored set is the frozen v1.1 release. Distribution through dbNSFP does not make dbNSFP this resource.

primary_purpose: Tissue-specific gene expression and eQTL context
technical_compatibility: Web/API/data downloads. Which builds are available depends on the resource release.
selection_rationale: Included because tissue-specific expression context can inform biological plausibility and regulatory interpretation.
appropriate_use: Use when relevant tissues and biological context are available.
interpretation_boundary: Expression context does not independently establish variant pathogenicity.
key_limitations: Donor composition, tissue availability, context dependence, and association limitations.

primary_purpose: Functional genomic annotations and regulatory-element context
selection_rationale: Included for experimentally derived functional-genomic context around noncoding or regulatory variants.
appropriate_use: Use when genomic coordinates overlap relevant regulatory annotations.
interpretation_boundary: Annotation overlap does not prove disease mechanism or clinical impact.
key_limitations: Cell-type and experimental-context specificity; incomplete coverage.

selection_rationale: Included as an integrative entry point for regulatory annotation.
appropriate_use: Use for hypothesis generation regarding regulatory context.
interpretation_boundary: Scores are not direct clinical pathogenicity evidence.
key_limitations: Evidence aggregation and tissue/context limitations.

selection_rationale: Included as a complementary functional-genomics resource for promoter/enhancer and expression context.
appropriate_use: Use when relevant cell-type or regulatory annotation is needed.
interpretation_boundary: Does not by itself establish variant effect or causality.
key_limitations: Coverage and context dependence; update status must be checked.

primary_purpose: Protein function, domains, sequence features, and curated annotations
selection_rationale: Included for curated protein-function and domain context relevant to variant interpretation.
appropriate_use: Use when a variant can be mapped reliably to a protein sequence and functional feature.
interpretation_boundary: Protein annotation alone does not determine clinical significance.
key_limitations: Annotation completeness and isoform mapping can vary.

selection_rationale: Included where experimentally resolved structure can inform residue-level or domain-level context.
appropriate_use: Use when reliable structural coverage and mapping are available.
interpretation_boundary: Structure presence does not prove functional or clinical impact.
key_limitations: Incomplete protein coverage; construct and experimental context limitations.

selection_rationale: Included for structural hypothesis generation when experimental structures are unavailable.
appropriate_use: Use with confidence measures and in conjunction with known protein biology.
interpretation_boundary: Predicted structure is not direct functional or clinical evidence.
key_limitations: Prediction confidence, conformational dynamics, complexes, and mapping limitations.

primary_purpose: Protein families, domains, and functional sites
selection_rationale: Included for standardized domain and family context during protein-level interpretation.
appropriate_use: Use when variant localization relative to known domains is relevant.
interpretation_boundary: Domain overlap alone does not establish pathogenicity.
key_limitations: Annotation coverage and functional specificity vary.

primary_purpose: Phenotype- and gene-level retrieval for mitochondrial disease
input: Phenotype, gene, and variant queries related to mitochondrial disease
output: Mitochondrial-disease knowledge retrieval and prioritization context
selection_rationale: Included because MSeqDR provides mitochondrial-disease phenotype, gene, and variant context when that disease group is part of the clinical question.
appropriate_use: Use for prioritization when the differential includes mitochondrial disease, and review the underlying sources returned by the query.
interpretation_boundary: A mitochondrial-disease query result does not establish causality and is not a classification.
key_limitations: Scope is mitochondrial disease rather than general Mendelian interpretation. Coverage, update timing, and dependence on upstream databases have to be reviewed.

primary_purpose: Orchestrated filtering and prioritization of germline variants
technical_compatibility: Web platform; VCF and optional pedigree or control inputs. The public site is served over HTTP.
selection_rationale: Included as a representative cloud workflow that can filter and prioritize germline variants from a VCF using a saved recipe. Component databases and predictors still have to be appraised on their own.
appropriate_use: Use when the documented inputs, recipe, and version fit the case, including optional pedigree or control files.
interpretation_boundary: A prioritized list does not establish gene–disease validity, a splice effect, or a clinical classification.
key_limitations: Results depend on the selected filters, predictor thresholds, and embedded data releases. Concordance among embedded predictors is not independent evidence.

analytical_function: Clinical evidence retrieval and curation;Reporting, documentation, and reinterpretation
primary_purpose: Submitted clinical variant interpretations and supporting assertion context
output: Clinical significance submissions, review status, conflicts
selection_rationale: Included to retrieve prior clinical assertions, review status, conflicts, and associated evidence context.
appropriate_use: Use when reviewing previously reported clinical interpretations.
interpretation_boundary: Entries are not definitive conclusions and must be appraised in context.
key_limitations: Conflicting submissions, variable review status, curation lag, and heterogeneous evidence.

primary_purpose: Curated literature-derived human gene mutation information
selection_rationale: Included as a literature-derived variant resource that may support evidence retrieval where access is available.
appropriate_use: Use as a starting point for primary-literature verification.
interpretation_boundary: A reported disease association is not a final classification.
key_limitations: Subscription access, curation criteria, and need for primary-source appraisal.

primary_purpose: Genomic literature search and variant/gene evidence retrieval
output: Literature links and indexed evidence context
technical_compatibility: Web platform; query based. Coordinate queries depend on the build used for variant normalization.
selection_rationale: Included to support efficient retrieval of relevant published evidence.
appropriate_use: Use to identify literature for direct appraisal.
interpretation_boundary: Search results do not replace assessment of study quality or applicability.
key_limitations: Indexing scope, access tier, normalization, and literature quality vary.

output: Bibliographic records and links to literature
selection_rationale: Included as a core bibliographic source for retrieving primary studies, guidelines, and resource documentation.
appropriate_use: Use for direct appraisal of source evidence.
interpretation_boundary: Search retrieval is not evidence appraisal or clinical classification.
key_limitations: Indexing, query design, publication bias, and access limitations.

selection_rationale: Included because formal clinical classification should follow the 2015 ACMG/AMP joint consensus recommendation. Applicable ClinGen specifications are catalogued as a separate entry.
appropriate_use: Use after evidence selection and appraisal within defined gene–disease/inheritance context.
interpretation_boundary: Criteria do not replace evidence quality review, clinical context, or expert judgment.
key_limitations: General framework requires contextual and gene/disease-specific application.

primary_purpose: Gene- and disease-specific ACMG/AMP specifications where available
selection_rationale: Included because applicable expert specifications can improve consistency of ACMG/AMP criteria application.
appropriate_use: Use when a current, applicable specification exists.
interpretation_boundary: Absence of a specification does not justify overinterpretation.
key_limitations: Coverage is incomplete; applicability and version must be checked.

primary_purpose: Computational support for ACMG/AMP evidence aggregation
technical_compatibility: Variant annotations; command-line. Web interface: wInterVar (https://wintervar.wglab.org/).
selection_rationale: Included as a representative tool that can organize ACMG/AMP evidence for review.
appropriate_use: Use as a structured aid with current specifications and expert review.
interpretation_boundary: Automated suggestions are not final clinical classifications.
key_limitations: Rule implementation, versioning, and context-specific criteria limitations.

primary_purpose: Variant annotation and ACMG/AMP interpretation support
selection_rationale: Included as a representative integrated annotation and classification-support platform.
appropriate_use: Use with transparent review of evidence, criteria activation, and current specifications.
interpretation_boundary: Platform output is not a substitute for expert clinical review.
key_limitations: Underlying data updates, rule implementation, and source dependence.

primary_purpose: Variant classification support and evidence review
selection_rationale: Included as a representative classification-support platform.
appropriate_use: Use as a support tool alongside manual evidence appraisal and applicable specifications.
interpretation_boundary: Do not accept automated classifications without contextual review.
key_limitations: Evidence aggregation, versioning, and implementation differences.

primary_purpose: Technical standard for validation, interpretation, and reporting of constitutional next-generation sequencing
input: Case evidence, classification, and laboratory context
selection_rationale: Included as the ACMG technical standard for constitutional gene-panel, exome, and genome sequencing, including what a clinical report should document. It is a different document from the 2015 ACMG/AMP classification framework.
appropriate_use: Use when recording methods, coverage, variant description, classification, limitations, and secondary-finding policy for a constitutional exome or genome report.
interpretation_boundary: The standard does not assign ACMG/AMP criteria to a variant and does not replace local or jurisdictional reporting rules.
key_limitations: This entry cites the 2021 revision. Later ACMG documents, CAP or ISO requirements, and laboratory procedures may also apply.
